claims.statement: ENV is a Make variable defaulting to local; ENV=staging layers docker-compose.staging.yml over docker-compose.yml, any other value is a make error, and ENV only changes which Postgres the local Docker tooling and containers use (it deploys nothing).

The staging overlay redefines only the backend DATABASE_URL from STAGING_DATABASE_URL or the STAGING_DB_* parts, using :? guards on host, user and password so an empty staging block fails fast instead of connecting to localhost; scripts/db-url.sh resolves the effective URL via 'compose config' so compose is the single source of truth for the connection string.

The local backend DATABASE_URL is built in keyword/value form from LOCAL_DB_* parts (overridable by LOCAL_DATABASE_URL, with POSTGRES_PASSWORD as legacy fallback), so passwords need no percent-encoding; the bundled Postgres only starts under the localdb compose profile and the backend's dependency on it is required:false so a managed DB can replace it.
STAGING_DB_* variables are local-tooling-only; the backend reads DATABASE_URL (Settings.database_url), so setting STAGING_DB_* on a deployed host has no effect.

make up and make seed are pinned to ENV=local for migrations: make up migrates only when ENV=local and the compose file has a postgres service (localdb profile), and seed depends on migrate only under ENV=local; against a managed database migrations are a separate deliberate 'make migrate ENV=staging' because the backend refuses to boot on an unmigrated database.
make up ENV=staging runs the local containers against the shared managed database, so a local research run writes directly into the database the deployed app serves.

The db-clean, db-reset, db-backup and db-upgrade targets are local-only (require_local refuses other ENV), while db-init-remote and db-push-remote refuse ENV=local and refuse to run against a database that already has an orgs table.

Supabase Storage configuration (SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY) is global rather than per-environment: with the backend on local Postgres, documents rows are local but archived objects land in the cloud bucket; ENV=staging puts both together, and staff-source is therefore staging-only.

Settings treats blank as default: a before-validator returns the field's declared default for a blank string on the model tiers, sql_audit_model, max_parallel_research, research_page_limit, research_model_call_limit, ask_model_call_limit, db_pool_max_size, db_pool_timeout_s, db_connect_timeout_s and db_statement_timeout_ms (None for the two research limits means no limit; ask_model_call_limit falls back to 25), because compose forwards unset variables as empty strings; dev_auth blank means False.

SQL_AUDIT_MODEL=off (case-insensitive) is normalised to an empty string, and build_agent only appends the answer_audit middleware when sql_audit_model is truthy, so the post-answer SQL audit is disabled; a blank value gets the Haiku default so the audit stays on.

Optional subsystems are enabled by derived Settings properties: auth_enabled when SUPABASE_URL is set (empty means every request resolves to the seeded dev user, except that with DEV_AUTH on a 'Bearer dev:<email>@local.test' header picks a seeded local test user), graph_enabled needs both NEO4J_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY, langfuse_enabled needs both Langfuse keys, storage_enabled needs SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY; unset, they degrade rather than crash (uploads return 503, archiving skipped).

DEV_AUTH is a local-only flag that must not be set on a deployed backend, and its effect depends on SUPABASE_URL: with auth enabled it makes 'Bearer dev' resolve to the dev user; with auth disabled it makes 'Bearer dev:<email>' resolve a seeded @local.test user that has an auth_user_id (other domains or unknown emails are 401).

db_gate_slots is max(2, DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE - 3) so concurrency gates sit under the shared pool, leaving room for the LangGraph checkpointer, which writes on every graph step; MAX_PARALLEL_RESEARCH and DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE should be raised together.

Only variables listed in the compose backend environment block reach the container (.env is not mounted into it), so unlisted Settings fields such as the NEWS_* tunables, SQL limits and MCP settings stay at code defaults in Docker, and NEO4J_URI/credentials and EMBEDDING_DIM are hard-coded in compose rather than taken from .env.

CORS is configured from ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated, default http://localhost:3000) and ALLOWED_ORIGIN_REGEX, and an empty regex is passed as None because an empty pattern would match every origin.

Langfuse tracing environment falls back to VERCEL_ENV and release to VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA when LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT/LANGFUSE_RELEASE are unset; LangSmith is switched on purely by process environment variables, and the boot log reports when it is half-configured.

Local ports: frontend 3000, backend 8010 published from container 8000, Postgres 5433 from 5432, Neo4j 7474/7687; make dev-backend runs uvicorn on the host at 8000 against localhost:5433, and the frontend uses AGENT_URL ending in /agent while NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL does not.
ASK_MODEL_CALL_LIMIT (default 25) caps the model calls one Ask question may make; compose forwards it and build_agent applies it via model_call_cap(settings.ask_model_call_limit).

DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_S (10 s wait for a pooled connection), DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S (5 s to open one) and DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS (15000 ms per REST statement run as the caller) are Settings fields that compose forwards and that blank resolves to their defaults; the pool/checkpointer and the statement-timeout pool consume them.
